app.title: RISING STAR MAKER
app.subtitle: Intern Mentorship Observation Console
app.tagline: Mentor one intern for three months, then see who they become.
app.intro: For the next three months, I will mentor a newly hired SDE intern. I do not yet know what they will be best at, and I do not plan to decide too early.
label.noAchievements: No achievements yet. Keep mentoring chaotically.
label.resultDeckCopy: All three activities are complete and archived. Move to next week, or take one more look at this set of outcomes.
label.monthlyReviewHint: Open this report to review the patterns and risks that have become visible so far.
label.nextRun: If You Want a Different Plan Next Run
confirm.clear: Clear current save data and the Intern Archive? This cannot be undone.
situation.feedback.opportunity: This plan landed at exactly the right time. {name}'s work got noticed faster than usual.
situation.feedback.risk: This plan ran straight into this week's problem, and even simple tasks picked up extra pitfalls.
situation.feedback.related: This plan did not address this week's issue head-on, but it still reinforced the same direction.
situation.release_cleanup.title: Pre-release Cleanup
situation.release_cleanup.description: A new version is about to ship, and everyone is cleaning up loose changes. We do not lack firefighters this week, we lack people willing to finish the final checks.
situation.docs_refresh.title: Documentation Needs Updating
situation.docs_refresh.description: Someone followed old docs and took the wrong path, and we realized several common manuals no longer match reality. Whoever touches it this week updates a section.
situation.new_teammate.title: A New Teammate Arrives
situation.new_teammate.description: A new teammate just joined and knows nothing about the business yet. Sometimes what someone truly understands only becomes clear after they explain it to another person.
situation.tech_debt_week.title: Tech Debt Cleanup Week
situation.tech_debt_week.description: No rush for new features this week. Everyone picked old issues that have sat around too long. Doing a lot is not the goal, do not fix one bug and create two more.
situation.quiet_week.title: A Rare Quiet Week
situation.quiet_week.description: No release and no incidents this week, so the calendar opened up. A good chance to catch up on missing basics or seriously try something long postponed.
situation.customer_visit.title: Customer Drop-In
situation.customer_visit.description: A customer suddenly asked to review what we have built recently. They do not care how much code we wrote, only whether their actual problem is solved.
situation.internal_tech_fair.title: Internal Tech Fair
situation.internal_tech_fair.description: Several booths are set up downstairs, and anyone can bring a laptop and present. Small tools that run get attention, and clearly explained failure stories get attention too.
situation.open_source_issue.title: A Real Issue Appears
situation.open_source_issue.description: A stranger opened an issue in the project, with reproduction steps clearer than some of our own bug reports. That means someone is truly using it!
situation.cross_team_invite.title: Neighbor Team Asks for Help
situation.cross_team_invite.description: Another team is stuck on a cross-service request and wants extra eyes. Nobody fully understands the whole chain, so we must piece clues together while asking around.
situation.research_seminar.title: Research Sharing Session
situation.research_seminar.description: The research team shared an experiment that is not finished yet. Even the presenter has no final answer, so asking how to validate is more useful than repeating conclusions.
situation.test_env_unstable.title: Test Environment Down Again
situation.test_env_unstable.description: The test environment works one moment and reboots itself the next. Errors are not always code problems, but we also cannot blame everything on the environment.
situation.requirement_shift.title: Requirements Changed Again
situation.requirement_shift.description: The feature is halfway done, then stakeholders suddenly changed goals. Earlier work is not all wasted, but blindly finishing the old plan will not work either.
situation.mentor_busy.title: Mentor Is Busy
situation.mentor_busy.description: This week I am tied up by reviews and incidents, so responses will be slower than usual. {name} has to move forward first and also judge when waiting for me is not an option.
situation.incident_wave.title: A Wave of Production Issues
situation.incident_wave.description: Several unrelated production issues piled up at once, and everyone is context-switching nonstop. Helping is good, but when things get chaotic, random changes are dangerous.
situation.team_disagreement.title: Design Disagreement
situation.team_disagreement.description: Two engineers both believe their solution is cleaner, and long discussion changed no minds. We need someone to untangle the actual differences first, picking sides does not help.
situation.project_spotlight.title: Hackathon Project Suddenly Gets Attention
situation.project_spotlight.description: Someone shared the Hackathon project in a large internal group, and traffic spiked immediately. The buzz may disappear tomorrow, or become the first real wave of users.
situation.flight_club_day.title: Flight Simulator Experience Day
situation.flight_club_day.description: A local flight club brought in a simulator, and anyone can try it during lunch. It has little to do with my current work, but some interests surface exactly in moments like this.
situation.customer_escalation.title: Customer Is Truly Upset
situation.customer_escalation.descriptio: An important customer came with full records and demanded answers. We must reproduce first, then separate facts from assumptions, we cannot answer quickly with guesses.
situation.research_collaboration.title: Research Team Needs Help
situation.research_collaboration.descrip: The research team wants one engineer to validate an idea. It may never ship, but each experiment step will be questioned carefully.
situation.team_reorg.title: Team Reorganization
situation.team_reorg.description: Projects and reporting lines are being rearranged while daily work continues. At times like this, everyone naturally starts thinking about where they are headed.
situation.mobile_launch.title: Mobile Release Push
situation.mobile_launch.description: Another group is short-handed for final mobile release work. Screens are small, but loading, touch interaction, and device-specific bugs are not.
situation.security_review.title: Security Review Gap
situation.security_review.description: A routine review found one operation has broader permissions than needed. There is no incident yet, but this kind of issue cannot wait until something breaks.
situation.data_migration.title: Legacy Data Migration
situation.data_migration.description: Data from an old system must move into new storage, but formats and constraints do not fully match. Finishing code is only the start, one missing row or one duplicate row is a failure.
situation.model_experiment.title: Model Experiment Needs Engineering Validation
situation.model_experiment.description: Research teammates have promising model results, but scripts are not reproducible yet. Someone must turn the idea into something repeatable and comparable.
situation.user_interviews.title: Sit In on User Interviews
situation.user_interviews.description: Product teammates scheduled sessions with real users about recent experiences. We do not need to defend the product immediately, first understand exactly where users got stuck.
activity.fix_bug.name: Bug Fixing
activity.fix_bug.description: Give the intern a low-risk issue with clear scope.
activity.build_feature.name: Feature Development
activity.build_feature.description: Let the intern independently own a new feature.
activity.write_tests.name: Test Writing
activity.write_tests.description: Add happy-path and edge-case tests for existing code.
activity.read_docs.name: Documentation Study
activity.read_docs.description: Set aside time to read docs and organize unclear points.
activity.pair_programming.name: Pair Programming
activity.pair_programming.description: Take turns coding with an engineer and explain each thought process.
activity.tech_talk.name: Tech Session
activity.tech_talk.description: Attend an internal session and allow Q&A afterward.
activity.team_lunch.name: Team Lunch
activity.team_lunch.description: Have lunch with the team, with no work agenda.
activity.mentor_1on1.name: Mentor 1:1
activity.mentor_1on1.description: Discuss progress, blockers, and next steps one-on-one.
activity.demo.name: Feature Demo
activity.demo.description: Do a pre-demo for the team on recently finished work.
activity.production_incident.name: Observe a Production Incident
activity.production_incident.description: Join live incident response under clear role boundaries.
activity.touch_kubernetes.name: Kubernetes Hands-On
activity.touch_kubernetes.description: Let the intern carefully modify and release one config.
activity.friday_project.name: Friday Side Project
activity.friday_project.description: Spend half a day building a self-chosen mini project.
achievement.delivery_convoy.name: Lunch Logistics Lead
achievement.delivery_convoy.description: There were too many team lunches. The intern now tracks meal deals better than sprint tasks.
achievement.quite_hungry.name: I feel quite hungry!
achievement.quite_hungry.description: All three weekly slots were Team Lunch. Velocity unknown, social calories maxed.
achievement.friday_grind_king.name: Friday Perpetual Motion
achievement.friday_grind_king.descriptio: Side projects hit double digits. Product docs now fear Friday afternoons.
achievement.dont_touch_production.name: Hands Off Production
achievement.dont_touch_production.descri: A major incident mistake happened during this run. The warning labels are bigger now.
achievement.route_planning_master.name: Air Route Strategist
achievement.route_planning_master.descri: Aviation references came up so often that the team now assumes every offsite means an airport.
achievement.fix_bug_grinder.name: Patch Combo
achievement.fix_bug_grinder.description: The intern fixed so many bugs that regression checks became instinct.
achievement.crud_hero.name: Feature Assembly Line
achievement.crud_hero.description: Feature tickets kept coming, and the intern delivered so steadily it looked like there were two of them.
achievement.test_marathon.name: Assertion Endurance
achievement.test_marathon.description: The intern wrote so many tests that even comments started sounding like assertions.
achievement.docs_master.name: Documentation Monk
achievement.docs_master.description: The intern stayed deep in documentation long enough to clean up even long-outdated pages.
achievement.duo_ranked.name: Permanent Duo Queue
achievement.duo_ranked.description: Pair-programming happened so often that people started calling the intern-and-mentor combo a permanent duo.
achievement.tech_standup_show.name: Tech Talk Show
achievement.tech_standup_show.descriptio: The intern joined and hosted enough sharing sessions that meeting-room mics practically wake up on cue.
achievement.release_gatekeeper.name: Release Guardian
achievement.release_gatekeeper.descripti: After many bug fixes and test passes, the intern now treats "verify before merge" as muscle memory.
achievement.counseling_room.name: 1:1 Counseling Office
achievement.counseling_room.description: Mentor 1:1s got so frequent that the air itself smells like retrospectives.
achievement.demo_perpetual.name: Demo Engine
achievement.demo_perpetual.description: Too many demos. The projector now recognizes the intern as the default presenter.
achievement.incident_growth.name: Incident Surfer
achievement.incident_growth.description: The intern observed so many incidents that they became instantly recognizable in on-call channels.
achievement.cloud_native_pro.name: Cloud Native Fiddler
achievement.cloud_native_pro.description: The intern worked in Kubernetes so frequently that even kubectl autocomplete felt familiar.
achievement.friday_hackathon_resident.de: With Friday side projects happening nonstop, everyone treated the intern as bonus content for the main roadmap.
achievement.grand_slam.name: Flawless Week
achievement.grand_slam.description: Three critical successes in one week, like rolling a perfect roguelike seed.
achievement.team_wipe.name: Party Wipe
achievement.team_wipe.description: All three weekly outcomes failed. Classic run start: learning mechanics first.
achievement.comeback_reversal.name: Clutch Comeback
achievement.comeback_reversal.descriptio: A critical failure turned into a high-grade recovery on the same activity. Chat screams scripted.
achievement.chaos_lord.name: Lord of Chaos
achievement.chaos_lord.description: Chaos stat broke the ceiling. The roadmap is now in wild mode.
achievement.cyber_zen.name: Zen Build
achievement.cyber_zen.description: Past mid-game and still low chaos. It's like the entire team installed noise cancellation.
achievement.scope_inflation.name: Scope Creep Sovereign
achievement.scope_inflation.description: Every "small tweak" evolved into a side quest with lore.
achievement.social_ceiling.name: Social Cap Reached
achievement.social_ceiling.description: Social stat maxed. Even elevator small talk now ships action items.
achievement.ten_thousand_whys.name: Infinite Why
achievement.ten_thousand_whys.descriptio: Curiosity maxed out. No conclusion survives without one more why.
achievement.solo_king.name: Solo Queue Champion
achievement.solo_king.description: Independence maxed out. Once assigned, tasks in the intern's hands moved straight into clear-the-map mode.
achievement.trait_hoarder.name: Trait Collector
achievement.trait_hoarder.description: So many traits unlocked that the intern skill tree is nearly full.
achievement.question_barrage.name: Question Multicaster
achievement.question_barrage.description: Question counter exploded; the "good question" emoji is now overclocked.
achievement.bug_street_sweeper.name: Bug Sweeper
achievement.bug_street_sweeper.descripti: Fix count crossed the threshold. The bug backlog now flinches when the intern logs in.
achievement.internship_survivor.name: 12-Week Survivor
achievement.internship_survivor.descript: The intern completed the full 12-week internship campaign. Whatever the ending, they earned the applause.
event.fix_bug.criticalFailure: I asked {name} to handle a low-risk bug first. {pronoun} only fixed surface symptoms, missed the root cause, and regression tests then reported two more problems. We rolled back production and traced everything again.
event.fix_bug.failure: {name}'s fix did not cover the original reproduction path at all. I asked {pronoun} to add tests before changing code, and it only passed on the second try.
event.fix_bug.success: After reproducing the issue, {name} found the missing edge case. The fix and tests were small, and I merged it after review.
event.fix_bug.criticalSuccess: After fixing the bug, {name} found three similar issues. {pronoun} confirmed impact scope and completed all tests in one pass.
event.build_feature.criticalFailure: {name} coded for two days without confirming requirements. During demo, we realized the direction was wrong. I kept reusable parts, but the rest had to be deleted and redone.
event.build_feature.failure: The feature ran, but {name} missed many checks. After I pointed them out in review, {pronoun} spent the whole afternoon filling gaps.
event.build_feature.success: {name} finished as agreed, added empty-state and error handling, and I only changed two variable names.
event.build_feature.criticalSuccess: {name} delivered early and also built a dashboard that explained the complex flow clearly. This strong example was later reused by the team.
event.write_tests.criticalFailure: {name}'s tests did not verify key outcomes, but still looked green because of heavy mocking. Real issues only surfaced after {pronoun} and I deleted and rewrote them together.
event.write_tests.failure: {name} only tested happy paths. I tried two edge inputs, and the first test {pronoun} added afterward failed immediately.
event.write_tests.success: {name} added tests for both main and error paths, with names that made expected behavior clear. Review passed in one round.
event.write_tests.criticalSuccess: {name} identified a long-running flaky test and confirmed concurrent state contamination as root cause. After the fix, the whole suite stabilized.
event.read_docs.criticalFailure: {name} followed documentation from three years ago and accidentally deleted local environment config. After I helped {pronoun} restore it, I added a deprecation warning at the top of the docs.
event.read_docs.failure: {name} read many pages but did not first define what to find. By afternoon recap, {pronoun} still mixed up two services.
event.read_docs.success: After reading the relevant docs, {name} could already explain the service path of a request on the next day.
event.read_docs.criticalSuccess: {name} noticed a mismatch between the documented examples and the real config, then tracked down a long-ignored configuration error.
event.pair_programming.criticalFailure: During pairing, {name} kept editing silently, ignored reminders, and finally overwrote changes the partner was validating. I paused the task and asked both to explain approaches first.
event.pair_programming.failure: {name} spent most of the time just watching. When asked whether the steps were clear, the answer was always yes, but the process still could not be repeated independently.
event.pair_programming.success: {name} asked directly when unsure, and could continue smoothly when it was {pronoun}'s turn to drive. The partner said the session went better than expected.
event.pair_programming.criticalSuccess: {name} spotted that both people understood the problem differently. {pronoun} used one concrete example to align them, and a half-day task finished in two hours.
event.tech_talk.criticalFailure: {name} went on stage without preparation, and halfway through discovered the demo would not run. The remaining time was spent debugging live. I asked {pronoun} to do a rehearsal next time.
event.tech_talk.failure: {name} wrote down many terms, but mixed up two concepts during Q&A. After the speaker corrected it, {pronoun} reorganized the notes.
event.tech_talk.success: After the session, {name} wrote a half-page summary in their own words. I reviewed it, and the core points were mostly correct.
event.tech_talk.criticalSuccess: {name} connected the talk with last week's production issue, and the suggestion raised was added to follow-up tasks by leadership.
event.team_lunch.criticalFailure: {name} joked about a teammate's accent, and the table went quiet. After lunch I told {pronoun} that comment made people uncomfortable, and {pronoun} apologized the same day.
event.team_lunch.failure: {name} interrupted others several times to finish personal stories. I reminded {pronoun} after lunch, and in the next conversation {pronoun} clearly held back and listened more.
event.team_lunch.success: {name} spoke little, but could pick up topics others offered and remembered several teammates' food preferences.
event.team_lunch.criticalSuccess: While talking about travel, {name} recognized an aircraft type outside the window. A previously quiet table turned lively, and everyone started sharing their most frequent flight routes.
event.mentor_1on1.criticalFailure: Only at 1:1 did {name} tell me {pronoun}'s task had been blocked for four days, while previous updates all said normal. I aligned with {pronoun} on when to ask for help going forward.
event.mentor_1on1.failure: I asked what {name} wanted to do next, and {pronoun} only said "anything is fine." We picked a very small goal first and will reassess next time.
event.mentor_1on1.success: {name} clearly explained what has gone well and what has not lately. We removed one item and gave one extra week to the part {pronoun} is truly interested in.
event.mentor_1on1.criticalSuccess: {name} came to 1:1 with a personal retrospective and next-month plan. Two items were better than my original plan, so I directly adopted {pronoun}'s version.
event.demo.criticalFailure: {name} merged changes at the last minute before pre-demo, startup failed on site, and no backup recording was prepared. The session had to end early.
event.demo.failure: The demo barely finished, but {name} kept reading code and never explained what problem was solved. Afterward I asked {pronoun} to rewrite the opening.
event.demo.success: {name} explained the feature clearly with one flowchart. A small issue appeared midway, but {pronoun} could explain the cause, and most audience questions were answered.
event.demo.criticalSuccess: During demo, someone asked a question {name} had not prepared for. {pronoun} validated it on the spot, confirmed a real gap, and proposed a practical fix.
event.production_incident.criticalFailur: I asked {name} to only verify logs, but {pronoun} directly deleted a production instance. Recovery happened only after the owner took over.
event.production_incident.failure: {name} posted AI-generated guesses as facts in the incident channel, and the team followed the wrong path for ten minutes. {pronoun} later corrected it proactively and added evidence.
event.production_incident.success: {name} verified logs and organized time, request, and error codes without overreaching conclusions. This record helped the owner eliminate one path.
event.production_incident.criticalSucces: {name} spotted the same request identifier across two log sets and traced it to a bad config. After owner confirmation, rollback completed quickly.
event.touch_kubernetes.criticalFailure: {name} ran a delete command in the wrong namespace, causing six minutes of service outage. After restoring resources, we added clearer environment hints and permission limits.
event.touch_kubernetes.failure: {name} changed config but forgot to verify rollout status. We only noticed thirty minutes later that new instances had never started.
event.touch_kubernetes.success: {name} verified environment before submitting config, then checked instances and logs after release. I did not need to take over.
event.touch_kubernetes.criticalSuccess: {name} identified the issue as resource limits rather than application logic. {pronoun} validated with minimal changes and documented full steps.
event.friday_project.criticalFailure: For a side project, {name} changed a shared library without notifying anyone, affecting two teammates' online environments that afternoon. I asked {pronoun} to restore scripts first, then explain what happened.
event.friday_project.failure: {name} spent half a day setting up many folders, but core features never ran. In retro, {pronoun} admitted the initial scope was too big.
event.friday_project.success: {name} built a small tool that solved a personal pain point. It had few features but was immediately usable, with a sample set of flight-route data.
event.friday_project.criticalSuccess: {name}'s flight simulator plugin started as a hobby project. After demo, three teammates offered to co-maintain it, and {pronoun} added contribution notes that day.
trait.curious.name: Curious Mind
trait.curious.description: I noticed that after getting an answer, {pronoun} usually asks one more why.
trait.bug_hunter.name: Bug Hunter
trait.bug_hunter.description: When an issue is reliably reproducible, {pronoun} rarely changes direction halfway.
trait.doc_goblin.name: Documentation Expert
trait.doc_goblin.description: {pronoun} often updates docs proactively and explains the basis of each change.
trait.test_guardian.name: Test Guardian
trait.test_guardian.description: {pronoun} has started adding tests before touching code.
trait.coffee_powered.name: Coffee-Powered
trait.coffee_powered.description: I noticed {pronoun} picked up many cross-team details in the pantry.
trait.meeting_goblin.name: Meeting Conductor
trait.meeting_goblin.description: {pronoun} can restate disagreements and dares to steer meetings back on track.
trait.architecture_brain.name: Architecture Brain
trait.architecture_brain.description: When reviewing local changes, {pronoun} proactively checks upstream and downstream impact.
trait.open_source_addict.name: Open Source Addict
trait.open_source_addict.description: {pronoun} has started taking strangers' issues and patch suggestions seriously.
trait.startup_dreamer.name: Startup Dreamer
trait.startup_dreamer.description: {pronoun} has documented many product ideas, and a few already run as working versions.
trait.kubernetes_believer.name: Kubernetes Believer
trait.kubernetes_believer.description: When problems appear, {pronoun} now checks deployment status and resource limits first.
trait.aviation_nerd.name: Aviation Nerd
trait.aviation_nerd.description: {pronoun} can go from airport codes to routes, aircraft types, and flight simulation.
trait.chaotic_good.name: Chaotic Good
trait.chaotic_good.description: {pronoun} often deviates from plan. Results are unstable, but some unattended issues did get solved.
ending.no_return_offer.name: No Return Offer
ending.no_return_offer.description: Over three months, too many tasks from {name} failed to meet role expectations. I cannot recommend a return offer for {pronoun}, but that does not mean {pronoun} is unfit for all work.
ending.no_return_offer.summary.a: I sent {name} openings from several companies still hiring, some with work styles that may fit {pronoun} better.
ending.no_return_offer.summary.b: In the final 1:1, I explained the decision honestly and promised to keep helping {name} with resume and interviews.
ending.software.name: Software Engineer
ending.software.description: By internship end, {pronoun} can independently handle clearly scoped tasks and knows when to ask for help.
ending.software.summary.a: Without dramatic twists, {name} completed most assigned work and learned to check boundaries after several rework cycles.
ending.software.summary.b: I still do not know where {name} will be in a few years, but right now I can trust {pronoun} with a normal task.
ending.product.name: Product Manager
ending.product.description: When building features, {name} keeps asking who will use this and why. I suggest {pronoun} continue in engineering work closer to users.
ending.product.summary.a: {name} did not always write the most code, but in requirement discussions {pronoun} repeatedly asked questions that affected real usage.
ending.product.summary.b: My strongest impression of {name} is that {pronoun} is willing to admit requirements are unclear instead of rushing into coding.
ending.research.name: Researcher
ending.research.description: {name} invests longest in problems without standard answers. I suggest {pronoun} try a research-engineering direction.
ending.research.summary.a: Some questions were not solved by {name}, but {pronoun} documented conditions, failed results, and next steps.
ending.research.summary.b: I am not sure whether {name} will enjoy long-term research, but {pronoun} can tolerate periods without conclusions.
ending.technical_sales.name: Technical Sales
ending.technical_sales.description: {name} may not be the strongest coder, but quickly understands customer pain points and explains technical plans in ways people want to hear.
ending.technical_sales.summary.a: I introduced {name} to the sales team. After the first customer meeting shadow, {pronoun} brought back more questions than answers.
ending.technical_sales.summary.b: {name} did not finish the original SDE route, yet {pronoun} still translates between people and technology every day.
ending.developer_relations.name: Developer Relations
ending.developer_relations.description: {name} enjoys exploring tech and is willing to write tutorials, run demos, and answer community questions. I suggest {pronoun} try Developer Relations.
ending.developer_relations.summary.a: After {name}'s first tutorial was published, several corrections arrived. {pronoun} verified each one and updated content the same day.
ending.developer_relations.summary.b: Compared with finishing one feature alone, {name} is better at helping a crowd understand how to use that feature.
ending.staff.name: Staff Engineer
ending.staff.description: {name} has started watching dependencies between tasks and team collaboration patterns. Staff is still far away, but the direction is clear.
ending.staff.summary.a: {name} made several mistakes by focusing only locally, then {pronoun} began mapping upstream and downstream before implementing.
ending.staff.summary.b: My final advice to {name}: keep broadening perspective, and do not call yourself an architect too early.
ending.open_source.name: Open Source Maintainer
ending.open_source.description: {name}'s side project already has external users, and {pronoun} now spends more time responding to issues than writing new features.
ending.open_source.summary.a: The project is still small and had rough releases, but people are willing to maintain it even beyond {name}.
ending.open_source.summary.b: I originally treated it as practice, but {name} seriously learned release, rollback, and how to respond to criticism from strangers.
ending.founder.name: Founder
ending.founder.description: {name} decided to keep building a product after graduation. Right now there is only one usable version and a handful of users willing to give feedback.
ending.founder.summary.a: I reminded {name} that both cash flow and users are still uncertain. After hearing that, {pronoun} still chose to try for six months.
ending.founder.summary.b: It may not become a company, and might shut down in three months, but {name} wants to verify it personally.
ending.flight.name: Pilot
ending.flight.description: {name} ultimately did not apply for engineering roles. {pronoun} enrolled in pilot training and continues maintaining a simulator plugin.
ending.flight.summary.a: I started by mentoring an engineering intern, but ended up writing a recommendation letter for {name}'s flight school application.
ending.flight.summary.b: Looking back, those sudden airport-code mentions were not random topics. I simply did not read the signs at the time.
ending.kubernetes.name: Kubernetes Specialist
ending.kubernetes.description: After mistaken deletions, rollbacks, and several successful recoveries, {name} chose platform engineering. {pronoun} now checks desired state against actual state first.
ending.kubernetes.summary.a: I do not support {name} blaming every problem on the k8s cluster, but I have to admit {pronoun}'s recent judgments were right.
ending.kubernetes.summary.b: The team now routes complex deployment issues to {name}, while also requiring {pronoun} to get peer review before every operation.
ending.internship_extended.name: Internship Extended
ending.internship_extended.description: {name} had substantial rework early on, then improved gradually. I still cannot recommend direct conversion, but I am willing to give {pronoun} more time.
ending.internship_extended.summary.a: We wrote down the remaining capabilities and metrics to prove, and agreed how to evaluate at that point. This decision will not be delayed indefinitely.
ending.internship_extended.summary.b: {name} knows this is the final chance. {pronoun}'s recent progress is worth another observation period.
ending.frontend.name: Frontend Engineer
ending.frontend.description: {name} notices what users see and how they interact, and is willing to refine awkward details.
ending.frontend.summary.a: After several demos, {name} learned to walk the flow from a user perspective first instead of only checking whether functions run.
ending.frontend.summary.b: I suggest {pronoun} continue strengthening engineering fundamentals while doing more UI and interaction work.
ending.backend.name: Backend Engineer
ending.backend.description: {name} has become increasingly steady with service logic, edge cases, and production issues, suitable for deeper backend work.
ending.backend.summary.a: {pronoun} now knows a request is not just success response. State, retries, and failure recovery also need ownership.
ending.backend.summary.b: I am now willing to assign a clearly scoped service change to {name}, and let {pronoun} track behavior after release.
ending.mobile.name: Mobile Engineer
ending.mobile.description: After that mobile release, {name} began taking device differences, touch experience, and resource constraints seriously.
ending.mobile.summary.a: For the first time, {pronoun} realized the same feature can feel very different across devices.
ending.mobile.summary.b: After the release ended, {name} kept researching these issues. Mobile became {pronoun}'s chosen path.
ending.test_engineer.name: Test Engineer
ending.test_engineer.description: {name}'s most stable contribution is turning vague worries into repeatable tests, exposing issues earlier.
ending.test_engineer.summary.a: Before modifying complex code, the team now asks {name} which path is easiest to miss.
ending.test_engineer.summary.b: When finding problems, {pronoun} also provides reproduction methods, giving everyone more confidence to change legacy systems.
ending.security.name: Security Engineer
ending.security.description: A security review made {name} notice permission and trust boundaries. Gaps that have not caused incidents still cannot be ignored.
ending.security.summary.a: {pronoun} confirms whether risk is real first, then proposes minimal fixes, instead of labeling every anomaly as security.
ending.security.summary.b: I suggest {name} continue learning offense-defense fundamentals and keep this same caution while investigating.
ending.performance.name: Performance Engineer
ending.performance.description: When systems slow down or become unstable, {name} first clarifies how to measure, then narrows scope step by step.
ending.performance.summary.a: Several experiments brought no improvements, but data left by {pronoun} prevented the team from repeating the same detours.
ending.performance.summary.b: I suggest {name} continue work that demands patient measurement, validation, and deep system understanding.
ending.site_reliability.name: Site Reliability Engineer
ending.site_reliability.description: After several production incidents, {name} no longer asks only why services failed, but also how to prevent repeat failures.
ending.site_reliability.summary.a: In incidents, {pronoun} no longer rushes to speak, but first organizes timeline, impact, and reversible actions.
ending.site_reliability.summary.b: Reliability work is not flashy, but the team is already willing to include {name} in next on-call preparation.
ending.data_engineer.name: Data Engineer
ending.data_engineer.description: That migration made {name} realize one successful pipeline run is far from enough. Every run must be trustworthy.
ending.data_engineer.summary.a: {pronoun} checked duplicates, omissions, and mid-run failures separately, then rehearsed recovery once.
ending.data_engineer.summary.b: I suggest {name} continue engineering work around storage, pipelines, and data quality.
ending.ml_engineer.name: Machine Learning Engineer
ending.ml_engineer.description: {name} can turn model ideas into engineering workflows that run, compare, and ship, suitable for a continued MLE path.
ending.ml_engineer.summary.a: One impressive result did not make {pronoun} stop early. Reproduction steps, tests, and runtime conditions were all filled in later.
ending.ml_engineer.summary.b: Models will change and tools will change, but {name}'s ability to turn experiments into systems will keep compounding.
ending.data_scientist.name: Data Scientist
ending.data_scientist.description: {name} can extract testable questions from messy data. When results do not support the original hypothesis, {pronoun} knows when to stop.
ending.data_scientist.summary.a: {pronoun} ran analyses that ended without conclusions, but clearly stated what data was still missing, instead of forcing a story.
ending.data_scientist.summary.b: I suggest {name} continue learning statistics and experiment design, then practice on real business problems.
ending.applied_scientist.name: Applied Scientist
ending.applied_scientist.description: {name} is willing to study problems without ready-made answers and also willing to carry effective ideas step by step into real systems.
ending.applied_scientist.summary.a: During research collaboration, {pronoun} kept questioning whether methods were valid and handled engineering constraints seriously.
ending.applied_scientist.summary.b: This path needs deeper training, but {name} already shows patience for connecting experiments and production use.
ending.program_manager.name: Program Manager
ending.program_manager.description: {name} can organize disagreements, dependencies, and next actions so everyone knows what to do.
ending.program_manager.summary.a: In several multi-person collaborations, {pronoun} re-aligned scattered commitments and quickly found unowned gaps.
ending.program_manager.summary.b: I suggest {name} explore program management while keeping basic technical judgment.
ending.solutions_architect.name: Solutions Architect
ending.solutions_architect.description: {name} can first understand customer environment and constraints, then assemble multiple technical components into practical solutions.
ending.solutions_architect.summary.a: {pronoun} explicitly marked unclear areas on architecture diagrams and identified which integrations needed validation next.
ending.solutions_architect.summary.b: This role still needs years of experience, but {name} has already found interest between technology and real-world constraints.
ending.support_engineer.name: Support Engineer
ending.support_engineer.description: Facing angry customers and incomplete signals, {name} still reproduces patiently, gathers evidence, and drives resolution.
ending.support_engineer.summary.a: After receiving an issue, {pronoun} did not just forward messages, but followed through until a verifiable answer existed.
ending.support_engineer.summary.b: I suggest {name} take technical roles closer to customer environments, where this steadiness is needed.
ending.ux_researcher.name: UX Researcher
ending.ux_researcher.description: After observing user interviews, {name} started distinguishing what users say they want from where they actually struggle.
ending.ux_researcher.summary.a: {pronoun} learned to explain less and ask one more concrete example, and accepted that some feedback is naturally conflicting.
ending.ux_researcher.summary.b: I suggest {name} continue learning research methods and turn intuition into reliable observation.
ending.technical_writer.name: Technical Writer
ending.technical_writer.description: {name} can organize painful lessons clearly so others take fewer detours, and is willing to revise based on feedback.
ending.technical_writer.summary.a: {pronoun}'s documentation states assumptions and risks, and explains recovery steps when things fail.
ending.technical_writer.summary.b: When people hit issues now, they open guidance from {name} first instead of asking everywhere for entry points.
ending.programming_instructor.name: Programming Instructor
ending.programming_instructor.descriptio: When pairing or presenting, {name} is patient and can spot where others are truly stuck.
ending.programming_instructor.summary.a: After teaching, {pronoun} asks learners to do it hands-on once, then checks whether the explanation was actually clear.
ending.programming_instructor.summary.b: I suggest {name} try coding education while continuing to participate in real projects.
ending.independent_developer.name: Independent Developer
ending.independent_developer.description: {name} turned a free project into a standalone usable product, and handled non-code chores personally as well.
ending.independent_developer.summary.a: {pronoun} learned to cut unnecessary features and first deliver one complete version to a small user group.
ending.independent_developer.summary.b: It may not become a career, but {name} can already complete the full loop from idea to maintenance alone.
ending.no_return_offer.hint: This appears only when repeated rework, delayed help-seeking, and out-of-bound operations continue into late stages.
ending.internship_extended.hint: The first half went rough, but recent momentum is real. Another chance might be possible.
ending.software.hint: Stably fix bugs, build features, and write tests for several weeks. No need to rush for special labels.
ending.frontend.hint: Keep building features and demoing repeatedly. Notice details of how the product is seen and used.
ending.backend.hint: Handle more service logic, bug fixes, and production issues, then gradually own failure paths.
ending.mobile.hint: When mobile release opportunities appear, capture the moment with concrete features and demos.
ending.test_engineer.hint: Choose testing for many consecutive weeks so edge cases surface before users hit them.
ending.security.hint: When security reviews occur, identify trust boundaries using docs, tests, and incident experience.
ending.performance.hint: Read more, measure more, and use data to find exactly where the system is slow.
ending.site_reliability.hint: Join incidents repeatedly while continuing tests and retros for similar failures.
ending.kubernetes.hint: Keep near-stubborn interest in deployment state, and also solve real problems inside chaos.
ending.data_engineer.hint: When migration happens, prove you care about integrity, repeatability, and recovery.
ending.ml_engineer.hint: After model experiments appear, turn research ideas into runnable and testable engineering flows.
ending.data_scientist.hint: In messy migration signals, keep reading, questioning, and validating real business questions.
ending.applied_scientist.hint: When research collaboration appears, run experiments while pushing effective outputs into real use.
ending.research.hint: Read, ask, and share over time, and accept periods without standard answers.
ending.product.hint: Keep building features and doing 1:1s while repeatedly asking whose real problem this is.
ending.program_manager.hint: Through 1:1s, pairing, and daily collaboration, keep dependencies and disagreements clear.
ending.solutions_architect.hint: During customer visits, connect constraints, engineering implementation, and clear communication into one plan.
ending.technical_sales.hint: Demo frequently and engage teams, then practice translating customer issues into technical choices.
ending.technical_community.hint: Keep sharing, reading docs, and responding to others so technology becomes truly usable by more people.
ending.support_engineer.hint: After escalations, reproduce patiently and follow through until fix completion.
ending.ux_researcher.hint: When interviews happen, explain less for the product and ask more about real behavior.
ending.technical_writer.hint: Read and share heavily, turning your own path into a traceable entry point for others.
ending.programming_instructor.hint: Pair and share repeatedly until others can complete the next step independently.
ending.open_source.hint: Keep side projects alive long enough, and respond seriously to strangers' issues and patches.
ending.founder.hint: Beyond side projects, repeatedly build product, gather feedback, and own the outcome.
ending.independent_developer.hint: Give many Fridays to one direction and complete both build and maintenance alone.
ending.staff.hint: Observe upstream, downstream, and people dynamics first, not only pretty local code.
ending.flight.hint: Interests should recur across different activities until they influence real career decisions.
report.title.1: Month One: Still Learning How Work Happens Here
report.title.2: Month Two: Positive and risky patterns are now clear
report.title.4: Month Four: {pronoun} Starts Owning Work Independently
report.title.5: Month Five: Final Report Before the End-of-Internship Review
report.quiet: This month, {name} showed no standout extremes. Most tasks were completed on time, and a few still needed my reminders.
report.questions: {name} asked {count} questions in total. Some were basic, but a few genuinely changed our original approach.
report.docs: {name} organized {count} documents. Not all were fully accurate, but at least they left traceable references.
report.bugs: {name} handled {count} bugs. Some were fixed in one pass, others needed review or even rollback before they were right.
report.demos: {name} gave {count} demos. On-the-spot performance varied, but preparation started earlier than the first attempt.
report.projects: {name} started {count} side projects with very different completion levels. I still cannot tell which one will persist.
report.incidents: {name} joined {count} incident responses. Until {pronoun}'s judgment is more stable, I will still keep clear operation boundaries.
report.social: {name} left group activities early {count} times. I asked why, and in several cases it was simply a need for quiet time alone.
report.evidence.engineering: Across several coding tasks assigned to {name}, {pronoun} can now break down problems independently, complete changes, and return with results.
report.evidence.reliability: Before submitting, {name} checks boundaries and regressions instead of only the smoothest path.
report.evidence.research: When facing open-ended questions, {name} records hypotheses, validation process, and what still cannot be explained.
report.evidence.productSense: {name} now asks who a feature is for and what problem it truly solves, not only how to write code.
report.evidence.customerFacing: When facing customer questions, {name} first listens fully to what happened. If it can be explained on site, it gets clarified immediately; if uncertain, it is checked first.
report.evidence.communication: {name} is increasingly clear about personal understanding and verifies whether everyone means the same thing.
report.evidence.community: Documentation, talks, or mini tools from {name} are already being used and receiving concrete feedback.
report.evidence.ownership: When tasks are blocked or unclear, {name} proactively states current status and discusses next steps with attempted approaches in hand.
report.evidence.resilience: Some tasks were not done well by {name} on first try, but when similar issues returned, {pronoun} did not repeat the same mistakes.
report.evidence.incidentResponse: When production incidents happen, {name} first checks timeline, logs, and impact scope without turning guesses into conclusions.
report.evidence.leadership: During multi-person collaboration, {name} notices disagreements and gaps, and helps restate concrete next steps.
report.evidence.aviation: Aviation is not just an occasional topic for {name}. {pronoun} has brought this interest into projects and started letting it shape career choices.
report.risk.rework: Some tasks still expose gaps only after submission. I will continue observing whether {name} can verify key paths earlier.
report.risk.lateHelp: {name} has reported blockers too late before. Next stage requires earlier updates on what was already tried.
report.risk.unsafeAction: {name} once misjudged operation boundaries. Related tasks will continue with explicit limits and review.
report.risk.unclearCommunication: In several conversations, understanding was not aligned first, causing extra rework later.
report.risk.scopeCreep: {name} sometimes expands tasks beyond agreed scope, delaying core outcomes.
report.risk.none: No severe issue type has repeated recently. Still, I will continue monitoring whether {name} can stay consistent.
report.trend.growing: Over the last four weeks, {evidence} appears more often than before and no longer looks accidental.
report.trend.steady: {evidence} remains {name}'s most frequent direction, with little change across the latest four weeks.
report.trend.none: The last four weeks still lack enough stable positive records. I will continue observing what {name} does, without rushing to conclusions.
ending.nextRun.generic: Watch for weekly opportunities. Pick one related activity and repeat it for several weeks, and you may reach a different direction.
observation.1: During onboarding orientation, I saw {name} flipping through materials the whole time, then asking one question about return-offer criteria before it ended.
observation.2: {name} brought a paper notebook, but on day one only wrote down accounts and a few contacts.
observation.3: While the laptop was still installing updates, {name} had already asked about the difference between test and production environments.
observation.4: At the first team meeting, {name} got one person's name wrong, then corrected it personally before lunch.
observation.5: I asked {name} to review the repository first. After ten minutes of scanning folders, {pronoun} asked where the best entry point was.
observation.6: {name} directly said they had never used our stack. I noted it down and still do not label it good or bad yet.
observation.7: At the welcome lunch, {name} talked more than listened. I still cannot tell whether that is nerves or habit.
observation.8: On day one, {name} requested every permission visible in the system, though half are unnecessary for now.
observation.9: While receiving equipment, {name} forgot one adapter cable and only noticed before an afternoon meeting.
observation.10: Before asking the first question, {name} prepared reproduction steps and two screenshots.
observation.11: In the first stand-up, {name} listed every tiny action from yesterday and ran two minutes overtime.
observation.12: I asked what {name} hoped to learn by internship end, and {pronoun} said they did not know yet.
